rendered: The separated cathode powder was calcined in air at 600 °C[1] for 2 h[2]. The stated purpose was to remove surface coatings and carbon black (CB) from the powder: the calcination was meant to remove face coatings and CB[3]. The reasoning comes from the TGA-DTG data: the organic coating layer, which the authors suggest may form from a reaction between NMC622 particles and Cyrene, shows a ~3.3 wt% loss at ~350 °C[4], and the CB shows a ~4.1 wt% loss at ~550 °C[5]. Both can be removed by calcining in air at 600 °C[6]. After this calcination, the XRD patterns were nearly identical to those of the cathode rejects, with no impurity phases observed.
